result.summary: A narrow residential street with continuous sidewalks and mature street trees. The environment is characterized by brick row houses with several integrated garages, creating multiple conflict points where vehicles cross the pedestrian walkway.

hazards.name: Driveway conflict points
hazards.description: Multiple garage entrances on the left side require vehicles to cross the sidewalk, creating potential conflicts with pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street, mid-ground

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides limits sightlines between pedestrians attempting to cross and approaching drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near driveways and potential crossing points to improve visibility.

interventions.title: Raised Crosswalks
interventions.description: Implement raised crossings to slow vehicle speeds and reinforce pedestrian priority in this residential zone.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with brick row houses and a continuous, well-maintained sidewalk. While the environment is walkable, the lack of a buffer between the walkway and the parking lane, combined with visual obstructions from parked cars, presents standard urban pedestrian risks.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb line block the line of sight between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the travel lane.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical buffer, such as a planting strip or furniture zone, between the narrow sidewalk and the adjacent parking lane.
hazards.location_in_image: The interface between the sidewalk and the curb.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Introduce street trees or a furniture zone to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to narrow the perceived roadway width and provide space for street furniture or greenery, improving the pedestrian environment.

result.summary: This narrow urban street features sidewalks on both sides, though the walkway on the right is significantly constrained by the building edge and parked cars. The environment lacks physical buffers between pedestrians and vehicles, and a garage entrance on the left introduces a conflict point across the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Narrow Walkway
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the right side is extremely narrow and obstructed by signage, forcing pedestrians close to parked and moving vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street adjacent to the brick building

hazards.name: Driveway Conflict Point
hazards.description: A garage entrance on the left creates a point where vehicles cross the pedestrian path with potentially limited visibility.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or planting strip between the sidewalk and the roadway, increasing exposure to traffic.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the nearest intersection or mid-block to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Add street trees or planters to create a vertical buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway, improving pedestrian comfort and safety.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near the garage entrance and any potential crossing points to improve sightlines.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow residential street lined with brick row houses and a continuous sidewalk. While the street's narrow profile likely encourages lower vehicle speeds, the dense parallel parking creates significant visual obstructions between the sidewalk and the roadway.

hazards.name: Parked Vehicle Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking blocks the view between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the roadway, increasing risk during crossing.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line throughout the visible block.

interventions.title: Daylighting and Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces at intersections or mid-block crossing points and install curb extensions to improve visibility and reduce crossing distance.
